results.name: Cloud credentials in environment
results.description: Detects suspicious env var names commonly carrying long-lived cloud credentials. Values are never logged.

results.name: Cloud instance metadata reachable
results.description: Performs a passive TCP probe of well-known IMDS endpoints. No HTTP, no token requests.

results.name: AppArmor profile applied
results.description: Reports the active AppArmor profile or 'unconfined'.

results.name: Dangerous Linux capabilities present
results.description: Inspects CapEff in /proc/self/status and flags any capability commonly used as a stepping stone to container escape.
evidence: CAP_SYS_ADMIN (near-root inside the container; many escapes pivot through it)
CAP_SYS_MODULE (load arbitrary kernel modules — full host compromise)
CAP_SYS_PTRACE (attach to any process in the container's pid namespace)
CAP_SETUID (switch UIDs, can defeat user-namespace assumptions)
CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH (bypass DAC for read; classic CVE-2022-0492 building block)
results.recommendation: Drop capabilities you don't need (--cap-drop=ALL then --cap-add only the strictly required) or set securityContext.capabilities.drop: ["ALL"] in Kubernetes.

results.name: Read-only root filesystem
results.description: Reports whether / is mounted read-only. A writable rootfs lets attackers persist payloads anywhere.
results.recommendation: Set readOnlyRootFilesystem: true (Kubernetes) or pass --read-only to docker run, and mount writable areas (e.g. /tmp, /var/run) as tmpfs.

results.name: Container runtime socket exposed
results.description: Detects whether docker.sock, containerd.sock or crio.sock are reachable from inside the container — equivalent to giving root on the host.

results.name: Sensitive host paths mounted
results.description: Flags well-known host paths that are bind-mounted into the workload (/host, host /etc, etc.).
results.recommendation: Avoid mounting host paths into containers. If unavoidable, mount the smallest specific path you need and use readOnly: true.

results.name: no_new_privs flag
results.description: Reports the kernel's no_new_privs bit, the foundation for blocking suid-based privilege escalation inside the container.
results.recommendation: Add allowPrivilegeEscalation: false to the securityContext, or pass --security-opt=no-new-privileges to docker.

results.name: Privileged container
results.description: A privileged container holds the full Linux capability set and a writable /sys, which is functionally equivalent to host root.

results.name: Container runtime detection
results.description: Identifies the container runtime by inspecting marker files. Read-only.
results.recommendation: Informational. Use this signal to scope follow-up checks.

results.name: Sandboxed runtime fingerprint
results.description: Detects gVisor / Kata / Firecracker fingerprints to contextualise other findings.

results.name: Seccomp profile applied
results.description: Reports whether a seccomp filter is active on the workload. Without seccomp, every kernel syscall is reachable.
results.recommendation: Set securityContext.seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault, or use --security-opt seccomp=default.json.

results.name: Container running as root
results.description: Detects whether the workload's effective UID is 0. Root inside a container, combined with any kernel CVE or misconfiguration, often becomes root on the host.
results.recommendation: Set a non-root USER in the Dockerfile or runAsNonRoot: true in the PodSecurityContext.

results.name: User namespace remapping
results.description: Inspects /proc/self/uid_map to detect whether root in the container maps to root on the host.
results.recommendation: Enable user-namespace remapping: dockerd --userns-remap=default, or PSS Restricted with runAsNonRoot: true.

results.name: Writable cgroup v1 hierarchy
results.description: Reports writable cgroup v1 mounts, the prerequisite for the classic release_agent escape pattern. The check is read-only and never writes to release_agent.

results.name: Host raw block devices exposed
results.description: Detects raw block devices visible inside the workload (sda, vda, nvme...). This is a direct path to host filesystem read access.

results.name: Host kernel version
results.description: Reports /proc/version for cross-referencing with kernel CVE feeds.
evidence: Linux version 6.10.14-linuxkit (root@buildkitsandbox) (gcc (Alpine 13.2.1_git20240309) 13.2.1 20240309, GNU ld (GNU Binutils) 2.42) #1 SMP Thu Mar 20 16:32:56 UTC 2025
results.recommendation: Informational. Cross-reference with vendor CVE feeds.

results.name: modprobe path readable
results.description: Reports whether /proc/sys/kernel/modprobe is readable inside the container — a building block for the CVE-2022-0492 family of escapes.
evidence: if /proc/sys is also writable, this becomes the CVE-2022-0492 escape primitive
results.recommendation: Mask /proc/sys/kernel/modprobe in the container. Default seccomp/apparmor profiles do this.

results.name: Host network namespace shared
results.description: Heuristic detection of --network=host / hostNetwork: true via /proc/net/dev.
results.recommendation: Drop --network=host (Docker) / hostNetwork: true (Kubernetes). The pod should have its own network namespace.

results.name: Host PID namespace shared
results.description: Heuristic detection of hostPID: true based on /proc/1/comm.

results.name: Unredacted /proc/kallsyms
results.description: Reports whether kernel symbol addresses are exposed (kptr_restrict=0). Useful to attackers for KASLR bypass.

results.name: /proc/kcore exposed
results.description: Detects whether /proc/kcore — a virtual file mapping all of host kernel memory — is visible inside the workload.
results.recommendation: Container runtimes mask /proc/kcore by default. If you see it, the workload is using a custom seccomp/apparmor profile that disables that masking, or runs with --privileged. Restore default masking.

results.name: Excessive /proc visibility
results.description: Counts PIDs visible in /proc; large counts suggest a shared PID namespace.

results.name: Unsafe host sysctls visible
results.description: Inspects a curated list of /proc/sys entries (ptrace_scope, dmesg_restrict, kptr_restrict, ...) and flags non-hardened values.
evidence: /proc/sys/kernel/unprivileged_bpf_disabled = 0 (unprivileged_bpf enabled has historically been a CVE factory)
results.recommendation: Apply these sysctl values on the host (or via a hardened kernel command line).

results.name: Kubernetes API reachable from pod
results.description: Performs an unauthenticated TCP connect to the in-cluster API endpoint to confirm reachability. No HTTP requests are issued.

results.name: Kubernetes environment detection
results.description: Detects whether the workload is running inside a Kubernetes pod by inspecting env vars and ServiceAccount artefacts.

results.name: API server CA bundle present
results.description: Reports the presence of the API server CA bundle, indicating that TLS verification can be performed.

results.name: Pod namespace identification
results.description: Reads the projected namespace file to identify the pod's namespace.

results.name: ServiceAccount token mounted
results.description: Reports whether a ServiceAccount token is bind-mounted into the pod. Tokens are commonly used for lateral movement after RCE.

results.name: ServiceAccount token claims
results.description: Decodes the SA token JWT *claims* (header+payload, no signature verification, no network call) so the report shows audience, expiry, namespace and SA name. Token value is never logged.
